prompts.proposal_task:
Prepare a proposal from finished roundtable . Read its complete saved record at . Preserve the question, synthesis, ranked ideas, disagreements and open decisions as evidence. Inspect relevant project requirements and implementation before choosing the approach.
Write beside the saved record. Include the goal, plan, proposed tickets with functional Addresses and acceptance evidence, implementation order, dependencies and decisions that need the person. Proposed tickets remain prose in this file. Create no execution tickets, assign no implementers and start no execution. The person must review this proposal before any implementation request.
Publish the saved file with metaform roundtables submit . The page presents its exact revision for approval or rejection. Return the proposal path, its revision and verification on this planning ticket. This assignment delivers a proposal only.
prompts.connect: bring a question to a table of agents, follow it live, and read its result when it ends
prompts.instructions: roundtables opens a table of agents on a question, through the person's Roundtable 2 engine. The question is the table's whole frame: it is about no part and no project unless you give an Address, which focuses the table on that part. Open one with roundtables_open, giving the question as topic and the seats in speaking order (claude/<model>, codex/<model>, antigravity/<model> or an OpenRouter model id); each seat takes one agent slot. Follow it with roundtables_events after the last seq you read, and chair it with roundtables_comment, hold, continue, advance, reseat and end. Its answer is the host's summary, in roundtables_status. When it ends, the page shows every topic's synthesis and rankings, the final answer and links to the saved transcript. roundtables_status returns the same result without a system-agent report step.

prompts.opening_question:
A person brings you a question. It is the whole frame of this discussion: it is not about one part of anything unless it says so, and it may be about something that does not exist yet.

Build on what the others contribute, add what only you can add, and keep going until the question is answered.
